title: Application of Cryo-Electron Microscopy for Visualization of the Membrane-Associated Vesicles
content: Extracellular vesicles (EV) are small particles (from tens of nanometers to 1–2 μm in diameter) released from cells to the extracellular space; every EV is surrounded by a lipid bilayer. Several classes of EVs can be distinguished, including exosomes, microvesicles, and apoptotic bodies. EVs can be isolated from conditioned cell media and various physiological fluids, including blood plasma, urine and others [1]. A recent discovery has proved the existence of EVs attached to the outer membrane surface, they were called the membrane-associated vesicles (MAVs) [2]. The MAVs did not exhibit co-localization with the exosomal markers (proteins CD31, CD63 and others). So far, they have been described using optical microscopy [2,3] and atomic-force microscopy [4]. Despite a considerable experimental effort, the biological function of MAVs and their morphological characterization is lacking.
